title: Ensemble Adapter Manifest Schema
description: Schema for an adapter's `adapter.yaml` (TRD-2026-8d825f54 TRD-005, PRD REQ-005). An adapter is a provider skill directory (`SKILL.md` plus `adapter.yaml`) that implements one or more of the 14 toolchain categories. `adapter.yaml` declares the targeted contract version per category, the binaries and subcommand allowlist the runner may execute, the environment variable names it needs (never literal values, PRD REQ-022), health checks, detection signals, and the run-template plus output-mapping for each capability.

adapter.description: The adapter id, for example 'github' or 'plain-git'. Unique per (id, category) pair, not globally: one id may be split across several directories that declare one category each, so that each carries only the allowlist its own category needs. Resolution is keyed on (id, category), and `npm run validate` rejects the same pair in two directories.

version.description: The adapter's own release version (independent of the per-category contract versions it targets).

categories.description: The toolchain categories this adapter implements; one manifest may implement several (TRD interpretation I7).

contract.description: The 'major.minor' contract version this adapter targets, keyed by category; every entry in 'categories' must have a matching key here (PRD REQ-003).

binaries.description: Binary names this adapter invokes; every argv built from a capability's 'run' template must start with one of these.

bin.description: A binary from 'binaries' this allowlist entry governs.

sub.description: Subcommands of 'bin' the runner may execute (TRD-008 validateAllowlist).

allowlist.description: Per-binary subcommand allowlist; the runner rejects any argv whose binary-plus-subcommand pair is not listed here.

env.description: Required environment variable NAMES only, never literal values (PRD REQ-022, REQ-023); may be empty for adapters needing no credentials.

when.description: Optional language condition. The check runs only when the project is detected as one of the listed languages (marker-file scan of the project root, e.g. 'elixir', 'python', 'ruby'). A check without `when` always runs, and when no language can be detected every check runs too, so nothing that works today can regress.

minVersion.description: Optional minimum tool version (dotted numeric, e.g. '0.23.0'). A check declaring it is a version probe: preflight runs it FIRST, parses the version from its stdout, fails when the reported version is older (or unparsable), and records the reported version. TRD-2026-6995dc96 TRD-003.

versionPattern.description: Optional regular expression with exactly one capture group extracting the version from the check's stdout. Defaults to the first dotted x.y.z (with optional -prerelease) found. Only meaningful alongside minVersion.

arrayPath.description: Top-level key of the check's JSON stdout holding an array of objects.

match.description: Key/value pairs selecting the first array element to inspect.

field.description: Field of the selected element to test.

allow.description: Values of `field` that pass; anything else (or unparsable output, or no matching element) fails closed.

failMessage.description: Message reported verbatim on failure (the documented prerequisite).

jsonAssert.description: Optional JSON assertion on the check's stdout. TRD-2026-6995dc96 TRD-004 (kata binding gate).

health.description: Health checks preflight runs before any side-effecting capability (10s default elsewhere, per-adapter override here).

exitCodeNames.description: Optional map of the tool's non-zero exit codes to names (TRD-2026-6995dc96 TRD-029, PRD AC-017-2). A failing capability whose exit code is listed resolves TOOL_FAILED with 'exit <n> (<name>)' in the message and exitCode/exitName on the error, ahead of the tool's own stderr or stdout error envelope. Unlisted codes and adapters without this key behave exactly as before. Never makes any exit code a success.

detect.description: Detection signals used to auto-select this adapter when configuration does not name one; may be empty for adapters with no detectable signal (TRD interpretation I2).

short.description: Default bound in ms for capabilities of timeout class 'short' (read-only: list, single-item read, comment listing).

long.description: Default bound in ms for capabilities of timeout class 'long' (writes to the tracker and whole-backlog traversals). A project's `timeouts` in .ensemble/toolchain.yaml overrides both (TRD-2026-6995dc96 TRD-028, PRD REQ-017).

timeouts.description: Adapter-level per-class timeout bounds in ms. A class left unset falls back to the runner default (60000).

timeoutClass.description: Timeout class this capability is held to (default 'short'): 'short' for read-only capabilities, 'long' for writes and whole-backlog traversals. The bound is the project's configured value for the class, else this manifest's `timeouts`, else 60000 ms; every TIMEOUT error names the class and the bound (TRD-028, PRD AC-017-1).

module.description: In-process alternative to 'run' (TRD-2026-6995dc96 TRD-016): a JS file path RELATIVE to the adapter's own directory, loaded in-process by the work-graph dispatcher only after realpath confinement to that directory. Not executable through the argv runner.

export.description: Name of the function exported by 'module' (default 'run'); called as fn(capability, args, ctx).

run.description: Argv template; '${name}' placeholders are substituted with validated capability arguments (TRD-009), never interpreted by a shell.

inProgressWhen.description: Dotted path; after statusMap, a status of 'open' becomes 'in_progress' when this path resolves to a non-empty string (an owner). 'closed' never changes (TRD-034).

countFrom.description: Dotted path of the total the tool reports for a list read; the mapped item count must equal it or mapOutput throws BAD_OUTPUT naming truncation (TRD-029).

completeFrom.description: Dotted path of the tool's own 'complete' boolean; anything but true is refused as BAD_OUTPUT (TRD-029).

truncatedFrom.description: Dotted path of the tool's own 'truncated' boolean; anything but false is refused as BAD_OUTPUT (TRD-029).

parse.description: Output-mapping block: how the capability's stdout is parsed and projected to the category's normalized output shape.

variants.description: Optional per-capability variant run templates keyed by '<selectorArg>: {<value>: run[]}'; the selector arg must be declared as an input of this capability in its category contract (TRD-005 AC).

successExitCodes.description: Child process exit codes (beyond 0, which always succeeds) this capability's runner (`runCapability`) must still treat as a non-crash and continue mapping stdout for, instead of `TOOL_FAILED` (TRD-2026-8d825f54 PR 10 fix round, item 3). For example the shipped `test-runner.run` capability declares `[0, 1]` because its per-language runner scripts exit 1 to report a FAILING test suite, not a crash. Never implies success of the underlying operation by itself -- it only controls whether that exit code's stdout still gets parsed; an exit code outside this list, a signal, a timeout, or stdout that fails to parse at all still resolves `TOOL_FAILED`.

capabilities.description: Capabilities this adapter implements, keyed by '<category>.<capability>' (matching the category contract's capability ids, for example 'tracker.show').
